title: URAMP program terms: launch, application, license status, consent agreement, complaints and completion
rule_summary: The Unified Recovery and Monitoring Program's published pages state the following program terms. The program's overview page describes URAMP as a confidential, voluntary recovery and monitoring program for the boards and professions overseen by the Bureau of Health Professions Licensure, and states that the rehabilitation programs of a similar nature the Bureau previously established for the Board of Registration in Nursing (SARP) and the Board of Registration in Pharmacy (PSUD) transitioned to URAMP when it launched in December 2024. The URAMP Frequently Asked Questions page describes URAMP as a statewide unified recovery and monitoring program available to all healthcare professionals licensed by the Bureau, with applications available where they seek support for their mental health or substance use or are referred to the program by their licensing board. The URAMP Frequently Asked Questions page states that URAMP is established in accordance with Chapter 177 of the Acts of 2022, An Act Addressing Barriers to Care for Mental Health. The URAMP Guidance Manual defines URAMP as the program developed and governed by the Massachusetts Bureau of Health Professions Licensure, a structured program designed to assist licensed health care professionals with substance use and functional impairment due to a mental health condition that impairs safe practice. The URAMP Frequently Asked Questions page gives December 16, 2024 as the date URAMP launches and as the date from which the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's Pharmacy Substance Use Disorder Program (PSUD) and the Board of Registration in Nursing's Substance Addiction Recovery Program (SARP) transition to URAMP, which absorbs them, with all monitoring program participation managed by the URAMP team. It describes SARP and PSUD as confidential, voluntary programs for licensed healthcare professionals with substance use disorders that impact their practice, and URAMP as also a confidential, voluntary program, available as well to licensees with mental health concerns that are not related to substance use disorders and have the potential to impact their practice. An applicant obtains the application from URAMP staff by calling the confidential URAMP line, and shall be effectively enrolled within ninety days of starting the application process, a period the URAMP director may extend. Upon receipt of the application the applicant's license status is changed online by the licensing board to non-disciplinary restriction, meaning the applicant is not permitted to practice; that status is published in the licensee database without the reasons for it and remains upon effective enrollment. The manual describes URAMP as able to function as an alternative to disciplinary proceedings where evidence indicates that the incident happened as a result of, or in connection with, a substance use disorder or mental health condition, giving the licensee the opportunity to demonstrate, in a non-disciplinary and non-public manner, that the health condition can be managed so that the licensee can safely return to practice while retaining the license. When admission is being considered as an alternative to discipline the applicant is asked to sign a legally binding agreement not to practice during that period. While an application is pending the complaint resolution process continues, and where admission is not granted the case is remitted to the Bureau of Health Professions Licensure investigators to determine whether disciplinary proceedings are required. A referral by licensing board investigators may not mean entry into the program, and a referral is described as unlikely to be appropriate where a licensed health professional has diverted drugs for sale or distribution to others, caused harm to a patient because of their abuse, or engaged in behavior with a high potential for causing harm, such as substituting or tampering with patients' drugs. Applicants must admit to having problems with substance use and/or accept that mental health is currently impacting their practice, and agree to waive all rights to appeal, file grievances or complaints, and contest licensure actions relating to or arising from their URAMP participation. Participation is governed by the URAMP Consent Agreement for Participants, a legally binding document entered into as a condition of acceptance into the program, effective when countersigned by URAMP staff, by which the participant agrees to voluntarily surrender the license should the participant fail to successfully complete participation by withdrawal or by termination for noncompliance; a URAMP agreement runs five years with an opportunity for early discharge at the three-year mark. Upon effective enrollment, pending complaints based on facts related to the incidents that led to enrollment are dismissed by the licensing board without prejudice. A participant may withdraw at any point, and the licensing board will then proceed with disciplinary action in relation to the underlying complaint; noncompliance may result in a cease-to-practice order, an extension or modification of the agreement, termination from the program and a report to the licensing board; and at any point during participation the licensing board may obtain pertinent records of participation. Records pertaining to participation, including the application, are described as confidential and not subject to public records requests; participants admitted into URAMP are not reported in public or to any disciplinary database; participant matters heard before the rehabilitation evaluation committee and the licensing board are heard in executive session; and if an applicant decides not to participate after the application has been submitted, the information provided may be used by the licensing board in connection with a subsequent disciplinary action, only where it is relevant to the matter under investigation. When the licensing board has approved successful discharge, all URAMP records are sealed and any related complaints are dismissed, and upon successful completion program conditions end and the license status changes to current.
exam_relevance: Tests the program's own operating terms as published: the non-disciplinary restriction status that attaches on application, the consent agreement and its surrender term, dismissal without prejudice on effective enrollment, the consequence of withdrawal, and what successful discharge brings.

common_confusions: The non-disciplinary restriction status attaches when the application is received, not at the end of the program, and it means the applicant is not permitted to practice.

Dismissal on effective enrollment is described as without prejudice and reaches pending complaints based on facts related to the incidents that led to enrollment; a participant who withdraws faces disciplinary action on the underlying complaint.
PSUD was not continued alongside URAMP; it transitioned to URAMP, which is also available to licensees with mental health concerns that are not related to substance use disorders.
